goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The hard-coded 10 MB gate applies to attachments as well as images, silently blocking files that a site's configured attachment limit permits.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:155 — Animation preservation is selected from the extensionless tempfile path rather than the original GIF filename, so oversized animated GIFs are flattened despite the allow-animation setting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in uploads_controller.rb lines 63-68, the code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. The tempfile.path is used for the 'from' parameter. In optimized_image.rb line 155, the animation check is `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, which checks if the 'from' path ends with .GIF. However, tempfiles typically don't preserve the original file extension - they have paths like '/tmp/discourse-upload-image20231015-1234-abc'. So even if the original uploaded file was a GIF (checked via `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` where filename is the original name), the tempfile path won't end in .GIF, causing the animation check to fail and animated GIFs to be flattened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL uploads now impose an undocumented 10 MB ceiling regardless of the configured image limit, so callers cannot downsize remote images above that threshold.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that at line 55, the download limit is hardcoded to 10.megabytes instead of using SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The new downsizing logic (lines 63-69) only runs AFTER the download completes, so if a remote image is larger than 10MB, the download will fail before the downsizing can occur. This means the feature to 'allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced' won't work for API URL uploads above 10MB, which is a real functional limitation/defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second downsize definition replaces the width/height overload in Ruby, so existing five-argument callers now raise ArgumentError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two `downsize` method definitions in optimized_image.rb. The first at line 142-143 takes (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) - 5 arguments. The second at line 146-148 takes (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) - 4 arguments. In Ruby, the second definition will replace the first, so any existing code calling downsize with 5 arguments (width, height separately) will fail with ArgumentError. The diff itself shows the first downsize being modified but then a second downsize definition is added that overwrites it.

matched_golden_ids: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: passing a percentage string ("80%") to gifsicle's --resize-fit option, which expects WxH geometry format, causing animated image downsizing to fail when animated thumbnails are enabled. Both comments point to the same bug with the same technical details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Hard-coding 10 MB for every upload type rejects attachments allowed by a higher max_attachment_size_kb and permits doomed uploads when that setting is lower.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 182 changes from dynamically reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (which would use different settings for different upload types like images vs attachments) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means: 1) If max_attachment_size_kb is set higher than 10MB, valid attachments will be incorrectly rejected client-side. 2) If max_attachment_size_kb is set lower than 10MB, users will attempt uploads that will fail server-side. The finding correctly identifies this as a bug where the hardcoded value breaks the configurable behavior for different upload types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL uploads are now capped at 10 MB regardless of attachment settings, regressing configured attachment limits without any downsizing path for non-images.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 55 changes from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` for API URL downloads. The new downsizing logic (lines 63-69) only applies when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. For non-image attachments uploaded via API URL, they are now capped at 10MB regardless of what `max_attachment_size_kb` might be configured to. This is a regression for non-image files where the configured attachment limit could be different from 10MB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — A large upload can synchronously run five full conversion and optimization passes on the request thread, multiplying CPU and memory cost enough for upload traffic to exhaust web workers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new while loop at lines 63-67 that runs up to 5 iterations of OptimizedImage.downsize() synchronously on the request thread. Each iteration performs image conversion/optimization which is CPU and memory intensive. This is done for every large image upload, and since it's synchronous on the web worker thread, it could indeed exhaust web workers under upload traffic. This is a real performance/availability defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Swallowing download failures leaves tempfile nil and the later tempfile.size call raises before an error can be returned or published.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows on line 55: `tempfile = FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil`. If the download fails, tempfile is set to nil. Then on line 63, the code checks `if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0`, which safely handles nil. However, on line 72, `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` is called unconditionally. If tempfile is nil (download failed), calling `tempfile.size` will raise a NoMethodError. The `rescue nil` swallows the download error but doesn't prevent the subsequent nil dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The downsize result is ignored, so a failed in-place conversion is retried five times and processing continues with a potentially invalid or oversized tempfile.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 67: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` is called but its return value is not checked. Looking at the `optimize` method in optimized_image.rb, it calls `convert_with` which returns `false` if the conversion fails (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`). Since the return value is ignored in the controller, if downsize fails, the loop continues retrying 5 times with a potentially corrupted or unchanged file, and then processing continues with whatever state the tempfile is in. This is a real bug where failed conversions are not handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Any logged-in user can force five synchronous ImageMagick passes over a crafted 10 MB image before validation, enabling CPU or memory exhaustion through repeated uploads.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows: 1) Client-side validation is changed to allow 10MB uploads (hardcoded instead of using SiteSetting), 2) Server-side at line 63-69 adds a loop that runs up to 5 times calling OptimizedImage.downsize on images that exceed max_image_size_kb, 3) The download limit is also increased to 10.megabytes. This means any authenticated user can upload a 10MB image, and the server will synchronously run up to 5 ImageMagick operations before any size validation. This is a legitimate DoS vector - repeated uploads of large images could exhaust server CPU/memory resources.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — No regression test protects the existing four-argument downsize API, so the duplicate definition silently removes that signature and can break callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in optimized_image.rb, there are now two methods named `self.downsize` - one at line 142-144 taking (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and another at line 146-148 taking (from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby, the second definition will silently override the first, meaning the 4-argument version (max_width, max_height as separate params) is removed. The new code in uploads_controller.rb calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` with 3 positional args plus opts, which matches the new 3-arg signature. However, any existing callers using the old 4-argument signature (from, to, max_width, max_height) would break silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — No upload-validation test covers attachments with a configured limit above 10 MB, allowing this image-specific feature to regress valid attachment uploads.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a regression for attachment uploads when configured limit is above 10 MB. However, looking at the diff, the hardcoded 10 MB limit (10 * 1024 KB) is specifically for client-side validation, while the server-side code in uploads_controller.rb shows the image downsizing feature is specifically for images (FileHelper.is_image?(filename)). The finding conflates image handling with attachment handling and makes claims about test coverage that cannot be verified from the diff. The diff doesn't show any test files, so claims about missing test coverage are speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — The new resize loop has no integration coverage for threshold boundaries, repeated non-shrinking conversions, conversion failure, or animated images.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new resize loop (lines 63-68 in uploads_controller.rb) that iteratively downsizes images up to 5 times until they're under the size limit. This is non-trivial logic with several edge cases: (1) what if the image doesn't shrink after conversion (infinite-like loop until attempt exhausted), (2) what if OptimizedImage.downsize fails silently, (3) behavior with animated GIFs. The finding correctly identifies that this new functionality lacks test coverage for these specific scenarios. This is a legitimate concern about missing tests for newly added complex logic, not a hallucination.
